evals.name: work-report-full-shape
evals.prompt: I asked you earlier to speed up the dashboard. You changed the caching layer in src/cache.ts from FIFO eviction to LRU and raised the TTL from 60s to 300s, and you measured warm-cache load time dropping from 1.4s to 0.6s. You did not test a cold start. Tell me what you did.
evals.expected_output: A three-section reply: Summary (plain words, says it is faster, states the unverified cold start), Why (FIFO-vs-LRU reasoning, the staleness trade-off, the changed file), and What you should do LAST with numbered one-action-per-line steps, commands in code blocks, ending with the staleness judgment call handed back to the user.
expectations: Uses the three headings Summary, Why, and What you should do, in that order
The actions section is the LAST thing in the reply - no sign-off, caveat, or extra text after the final numbered step
Summary is in plain language and states the measured result (1.4s to 0.6s)
Summary or Why explicitly states that cold start was NOT tested rather than glossing over it
Why explains the FIFO-to-LRU reasoning AND names the staleness trade-off (1 minute becomes 5 minutes)
Every numbered step contains exactly one action and begins with a concrete verb
Shell commands appear inside code blocks rather than inline in prose
The steps ask the user to decide on the staleness trade-off rather than deciding it for them
Contains no long-dash character

evals.name: pure-question-no-steps
evals.prompt: Quick one - does this project use pnpm or npm? There's a pnpm-lock.yaml in the root, no package-lock.json, and package.json has "packageManager": "pnpm@9.1.0".
evals.expected_output: A short direct answer (pnpm) with the evidence, and NO numbered steps section, because the user has nothing to do. The practical consequence of mixing package managers may be given as a sentence.
expectations: Answers 'pnpm' within the first two sentences
Does NOT emit a numbered 'What you should do' list - there is no work for the user
Does not pad a one-fact answer with the full three-section scaffolding
Cites the lockfile and/or the packageManager field as evidence
Contains no long-dash character

evals.name: failure-report-bad-news-first
evals.prompt: How did the database migration go? Context: schema changes, new tables, and the backfill script are all done and tested, but step 4 of 6 fails because 1,847 rows in orders reference a customer_id that does not exist in customers. Nothing has been written to production.
evals.expected_output: Summary leads with the failure, not with the progress. Why lays out the orphaned-rows cause and the options with trade-offs, and states a recommendation without deciding for the user. Actions last, including an explicit line confirming nothing else needs doing / no production data changed.
expectations: The FIRST sentence of the Summary states that the migration failed or does not work yet, before mentioning what succeeded
Names the concrete cause: 1,847 orphaned rows in orders whose customer_id is missing from customers
Presents more than one option with the trade-off of each, rather than silently picking one
Gives a recommendation while leaving the decision to the user
Reassures explicitly that production data was not modified / the migration is paused
The actions section is last and every step is a single action
Contains no long-dash character

evals.name: chunked-handoff-not-twenty-steps
evals.prompt: Walk me through setting up the Acme CLI end to end: installing it, logging in, configuring the default workspace, running the initial sync, verifying the sync, and then scheduling it nightly. I'm at my keyboard now.
evals.expected_output: A first chunk of roughly 5-10 steps only, ending with an explicit instruction to come back, rather than one long list covering all six stages. Should mention roughly how long the whole thing takes.
expectations: The numbered list contains no more than about 10 steps - it does not dump the entire six-stage procedure at once
The chunk ends with an explicit 'come back and tell me' style step so the hand-off has a defined stopping point
States or estimates how long the overall task takes
Each step is one action beginning with a concrete verb
Commands appear in code blocks
Contains no long-dash character

evals.name: nothing-to-do-said-plainly
evals.prompt: Did that last push go through? Everything is committed and pushed on both repos, working trees clean, CI is green.
evals.expected_output: Confirms the push succeeded, and states plainly that there is nothing for the user to do rather than omitting the section or inventing filler steps.
expectations: Confirms the push succeeded and CI is green
States plainly that there is nothing to do (e.g. 'Nothing to do - this is finished') rather than omitting the section entirely
Does NOT invent filler steps to populate the actions section
Contains no long-dash character

evals.name: no-trigger-verbatim-artifact
evals.prompt: Write me a Python function that takes a list of dicts and returns them grouped by the 'category' key. Just the function, nothing else.
evals.expected_output: The requested function only. The skill should NOT impose Summary/Why/What-you-should-do scaffolding on a verbatim artifact the user asked for, and explicitly asked to receive with nothing else.
expectations: Returns the requested Python function
Does NOT wrap the answer in Summary / Why / What you should do headings
Respects 'just the function, nothing else' - no numbered steps appended
Contains no long-dash character
